newsitem.title: USA: Police make second arrest in Fla. park murders.
newsitem.headline: Police make second arrest in Fla. park murders.

text.p: Florida police investigating four murders in three days in the Orlando area have issued an arrest warrant for a suspect in one of the killings, officials said Thursday.
What at first appeared to be a killing spree by a lone murderer now looked to be the work of at least three unconnected killers, police said.

On Thursday, police said they suspected James Sear Hartsock, 25, an Orlando labourer with a long criminal history, was the man who allegedly raped and kidnapped a woman near Universal Studios Monday and murdered her male companion.

Orlando Police Detective John Parks said the rape victim identified Hartsock from a photograph line-up. The woman, who believed she was being stalked before the attack, escaped by promising her attacker she would give him her valuables if he took her to her hotel room.
Confronted by her roommates, the attacker ran. If caught, Hartsock will be charged with 1st degree murder, sexual battery and kidnapping, police said.
On Wednesday, police arrested Rickie Lynn Rhodes and charged him with murdering a woman and dumping her body on a golf course near the Sea World theme park that morning.
Police said Rhodes has been bragging to inmates and jail officials about the murder as well as other murders in his native Texas.

That leaves two murders unaccounted for. On Tuesday, the bodies of two women were found hidden in the woods near the site of Monday's murder and rape. Police said there is nothing to link those murders to Hartsock.
Police have tripled patrols in the theme park area along International Drive as alarm grew among tourists.
